matched-betting.title: Matched betting: extracting profit from welcome bonuses
matched-betting.metaTitle: Matched betting – how to exploit bookmaker bonuses
matched-betting.description: Matched betting explained: how to use welcome bonuses and free bets at licensed bookmakers to lock in a profit, and how it differs from sure bets.
matched-betting.intro: Matched betting is a technique for converting bookmakers' bonuses and free bets into real cash. By backing and laying the same event, you cover all outcomes so the result doesn't matter – what remains is a guaranteed profit from the bonus.

blocks.text: How matched betting works

When you claim a free bet or bonus, you place it on one outcome at a bookmaker and lay (bet against) the same outcome at a betting exchange or back the opposite result with another bookmaker. Because the free bet stakes nothing of your own money, you lock in most of its face value as profit regardless of which side wins.
Bonus terms and restrictions

Welcome bonuses carry different terms depending on the bookmaker and the country in which you're betting. Some regulated markets cap bonus amounts and limit wagering requirements to protect consumers. Always read the specific terms and conditions before you accept any offer, and only use bookmakers that are licensed in the country where you live.

items: Check the minimum odds required to unlock the bonus – many bookmakers set a floor of 1.80 or higher.
Note the expiry period so your bonus or free bet doesn't lapse unused.
Consider using sure bets (arbitrage bets) to meet turnover requirements with minimal risk.

blocks.text: Combining matched betting with sure bets

Sure bets are ideal for clearing bonus wagering requirements because you're not staking real money on a single outcome. Once you've met the rollover, you can carry on finding arbitrage opportunities without relying on promotions.

faq.q: Is matched betting legal?
faq.a: Yes. Exploiting bonuses within the bookmaker's published terms is perfectly legal. However, bookmakers reserve the right to withdraw offers or limit accounts if they believe you are not betting in the spirit of their promotions or if you breach the terms. Tax on betting winnings depends on your country, so check your local rules.

faq.q: How much are typical welcome bonuses worth?
faq.a: Bonus values and wagering requirements vary by bookmaker and jurisdiction. In some regulated markets, welcome offers may be capped – for instance with a maximum bonus amount in euros and a limit on the rollover, expressed as a multiple of the bonus. Always check the current terms at the bookmaker you choose, such as bet365, Unibet, William Hill or Betway, and confirm that it holds a valid licence in your country.

er-surebets-lovligt.title: Are surebets legal? Rules and tax considerations
er-surebets-lovligt.metaTitle: Are surebets legal? Rules, tax and bookmaker terms
er-surebets-lovligt.description: Is it legal to place surebets, and do you have to pay tax on winnings? Here are the rules and what bookmakers can do about arbitrage betting.
er-surebets-lovligt.intro: The short answer is yes. Placing surebets is legal in most jurisdictions. You are simply placing ordinary bets with licensed bookmakers and comparing odds to find the best value – nothing about this process is illegal.

blocks.text: What can bookmakers do?

Although surebets are legal, bookmakers do not welcome customers who consistently place guaranteed-profit bets. In their terms and conditions, they reserve the right to reduce maximum stakes, limit markets or restrict accounts. However, they must always return your deposited funds and pay out any valid winnings.
Do you have to pay tax on winnings?

Tax treatment of betting winnings varies by country. In some countries, winnings from operators licensed by your national gambling regulator are tax-free for the player, while in others they may be taxable. If you use offshore or unlicensed operators, the tax position may be different. Check the current tax rules where you live, or consult your local tax authority if you are unsure about your situation.

Only use bookmakers that are licensed where you live, by your national gambling regulator. This typically offers consumer protection from your gambling authority and can affect how your winnings are taxed, so check your local rules.
Responsible gambling

Even with surebets, it is important to maintain control over your gambling. Set deposit limits, and use your country's self-exclusion register if you need a break. If you need support, contact a recognised gambling helpline in your country.

faq.q: Can a bookmaker refuse to pay out winnings from a surebet?
faq.a: A bookmaker must pay out valid winnings. It can void a bet if there was an obvious error in the odds, and it can restrict the account going forward.

faq.q: Do I have to pay tax on surebet winnings?
faq.a: It depends on your country. Some countries treat winnings from licensed operators as tax-free for the player, while others may tax them. Check the current tax rules where you live.

undgaa-begraensning.title: How to avoid bookmaker limits and keep your accounts open longer
undgaa-begraensning.metaTitle: How to Avoid Bookmaker Limits – Arbing Guide 2026
undgaa-begraensning.description: How to avoid bookmaker limits as an arber: a betting strategy that looks natural, the best bookmakers for arbitrage betting and examples in €.
undgaa-begraensning.intro: To avoid bookmaker limits, you need to bet like a normal customer: round stakes, popular markets, a mix of regular bets and no instant reaction to every price drop. Soft bookmakers limit accounts that consistently beat the closing line. You cannot avoid it forever, but a smart betting strategy can keep your accounts open for months instead of weeks.

blocks.text: Why bookmakers limit accounts

Soft bookmakers make money from recreational bettors, not from customers who only take mispriced odds. Their risk systems look at patterns: do you bet on prices that drop shortly afterwards? Do you only bet obscure markets? Are your stakes calculated to the cent? Each of these signals raises your risk score.

items: **Beating the closing line:** the strongest signal. If your odds are consistently better than the final price, you get flagged.
**Uneven stakes:** €463.27 looks like a calculator. €460 looks like a person.
**Niche markets:** corners in the second division of a small league attract attention.
**Only withdrawing:** frequent withdrawals without bonuses or regular bets look professional.

blocks.text: Betting strategy that keeps your accounts open

items: **Round your stakes** to whole tens. The profit barely changes.
**Stick to mainstream markets:** major leagues, 1X2, over/under and match winner in tennis.
**Mix in normal bets:** a few small regular bets per week, ideally on big matches.
**Avoid extreme pricing errors:** surebets above 8–10% attract attention and are often voided anyway.
**Do not react instantly:** betting the second a price moves is a classic arber pattern.
**Spread your volume** across many bookmakers instead of hammering one.

blocks.title: Example: rounded stakes, total stake €1,000
blocks.note: The rounded stakes still lock in a profit on both results, and they look far more natural to the bookmaker.

blocks.text: Best bookmakers for arbitrage betting
A good arbitrage setup combines two types of bookmaker. Soft bookmakers offer the mispriced odds, and sharp bookmakers or exchanges accept large stakes without limiting winners.

items: **Soft bookmakers:** the source of most surebets, but they limit quickly. Use them carefully.
**Sharp bookmakers:** lower margins and high limits. Ideal for the second leg.
**Betting exchanges:** you bet against other users, so you are not limited for winning. Commission reduces the profit slightly.

blocks.text: Read the full overview of the [best bookmakers for surebets](/en/guides/best-bookmakers-for-surebets). Only use bookmakers that are licensed where you live.
What to do when an account is limited

items: **Withdraw your balance** if the account can no longer be used for surebets.
**Do not open a new account** under someone else's name. It breaks the terms and can lead to confiscated winnings.
**Move volume** to your other accounts and to sharp bookmakers or exchanges.
**Track per bookmaker:** a [bet tracker](/en/guides/bet-tracker) shows which accounts are worth protecting.

blocks.text: The more bookmakers you can use, the less volume each account needs. [BetTracker AI](/en) finds surebets across many bookmakers, so you can spread your bets and keep your accounts open longer.

faq.q: Can I avoid bookmaker limits completely?
faq.a: Not at soft bookmakers in the long run. But a natural betting pattern can delay limits by months, and sharp bookmakers and exchanges rarely limit at all.

faq.q: Is it legal for bookmakers to limit me?
faq.a: Yes, bookmakers can usually decide who they accept bets from. See [are surebets legal?](/en/guides/are-surebets-legal)

faq.q: How many bookmakers should I use?
faq.a: Five to ten is a good start. It spreads your volume and gives you more surebets to choose from.

surebet-beregner.title: Free surebet calculator: work out your stakes in seconds
surebet-beregner.description: Use a free surebet calculator to split your stake across two or three outcomes. The formula, examples in € and how to round stakes safely.
surebet-beregner.intro: A surebet calculator splits your total stake across every outcome so the payout is the same whatever happens. Enter the odds and your amount, and the calculator shows the stake per outcome, the payout and your profit in € and %. The formula is simple, but a calculator prevents mistakes when you only have minutes to place the bets.

blocks.text: How to calculate surebet stakes: the formula

First add up the inverse odds: 1/odds A + 1/odds B (+ 1/odds C for three outcomes). Call this total S. The stake on one outcome is total stake × 1/odds, divided by S. The payout is total stake divided by S.

items: **Stake per outcome:** total stake × (1/odds) ÷ S
**Payout:** total stake ÷ S

blocks.title: Example: two outcomes, total stake €1,500

blocks.text: Sports arbitrage with three outcomes
In football and ice hockey 1X2 markets, a third outcome goes into the same formula. By hand that gets tedious, and this is exactly where a calculator saves the most time.

blocks.title: Example: 1X2, total stake €1,000

blocks.text: Rounding and uneven stakes
Stakes like €740.97 look suspicious to a bookmaker. Round to whole euros or tens. If you round to €741 and €759, the profit stays at about €56, with only a few cents of difference between outcomes.

You can also skew the stakes on purpose. If you only cover your stake on one outcome, you win €0 there and more on the other. In the example above, €768.29 on A and €731.71 on B gives a profit of €113.41 if A wins and €0 if B wins.
Always calculate with the odds actually shown on your bet slip, not the ones from the scanner. Prices can shift by a tick between the scan and the click.
The surebet calculator as an everyday betting tool

items: **Before the bet:** check the sum of inverse odds is still below 1.
**During the bet:** recalculate if a price changes.
**After the bet:** log the result so you can track your ROI in a [bet tracker](/en/guides/bet-tracker).

faq.q: Why does the calculator show a negative profit?
faq.a: The sum of inverse odds is above 1, so there is no surebet. Most likely one of the prices has moved.

odds-beregner.title: How to use an odds calculator
odds-beregner.metaTitle: Odds calculator – convert odds to probability and winnings
odds-beregner.description: Learn to convert decimal odds to probability, calculate your potential winnings, and find the bookmaker's margin with an odds calculator.
odds-beregner.intro: An odds calculator turns odds into something you can use: how much you'll win, how likely the bookmaker thinks the outcome is, and how much the bookmaker is taking. Here are the three calculations you need to know.

blocks.text: 1. Potential winnings
With decimal odds, which most online bookmakers use, the payout is stake multiplied by odds. The profit is the payout minus the stake.

blocks.title: €200 stake at odds of 2.50

blocks.text: 2. Implied probability
The probability the bookmaker is working with is 1 divided by the odds. Odds of 2.50 equals 40%. If you believe the chance is higher, it's a value bet.
3. Bookmaker margin

Add up the implied probabilities for all outcomes. The total is over 100%, and the excess is the bookmaker margin. If the total is under 100% across different bookmakers, you have a surebet (also known as an arbitrage bet).

blocks.title: Tennis: odds of 1.85 and 1.95 at the same bookmaker
blocks.note: The lower the margin, the better odds you get as a punter.

blocks.text: Our free sure bet calculator does all three calculations for you and distributes the stake across multiple outcomes.

faq.q: How do you convert odds to a percentage?
faq.a: Divide 1 by the odds and multiply by 100. Odds of 2.00 equals 50%, and odds of 4.00 equals 25%.

faq.q: What's the difference between decimal odds and fractional odds?
faq.a: Decimal odds show the total payout per unit staked, e.g. 2.50. Fractional odds, such as 3/2, show only the profit. Most online bookmakers use decimal odds, though fractional odds remain common in the UK and Ireland.

value-betting-vs-surebets.title: Value betting vs surebets: what's the difference?
value-betting-vs-surebets.metaTitle: Value betting vs surebets – differences, risk & profit
value-betting-vs-surebets.description: Value betting and surebets both exploit mispriced odds but work differently. Compare risk, profit potential and which strategy suits your betting style.
value-betting-vs-surebets.intro: Both value betting and surebets exploit bookmakers' pricing errors. The key difference: surebets lock in guaranteed profit instantly, whilst value betting delivers profit over a large sample of bets.

blocks.text: What is value betting?

A value bet is a wager where the odds are higher than the true probability suggests. If a match is genuinely 50/50 and a bookmaker offers odds of 2.20, that's a value bet. You only bet on one outcome and can lose individual bets, but over time the edge delivers profit.
What is a surebet?
With a surebet (arbitrage bet) you back all outcomes across different bookmakers so you win regardless of the result. The profit per bet is smaller, but it's guaranteed on every trade.

blocks.title: Comparison
rows: Surebets: several · Value: one or more

blocks.text: Which strategy suits you?

items: Choose surebets if you want stable profit without large swings or drawdowns.
Choose value betting if you can tolerate losing runs and have a large enough bankroll to ride out variance.
Many combine both: surebets for steady income and value bets to maximise long-term edge.

blocks.text: If you're starting out, begin with surebets. You'll learn how bookmakers operate without risking large losses.

faq.q: Is value betting more profitable than surebets?
faq.a: Value betting can deliver higher profit over the long term, but with far greater variance. Surebets offer smaller, more stable profit on every bet.

faq.q: Do bookmakers limit your account with value betting too?
faq.a: Yes. Bookmakers limit winning customers regardless of strategy, though value betting can be slightly harder to detect because you also place losing bets.

bedste-bookmakere-til-surebets.title: Best bookmakers for surebets
bedste-bookmakere-til-surebets.description: Which bookmakers should you use for surebets? See what makes a good arbitrage betting bookmaker and how to build your portfolio of accounts.
bedste-bookmakere-til-surebets.intro: There isn't one single bookmaker that's best for surebets. Arbitrage betting opportunities arise between bookmakers, so the most important thing is to have accounts with several operators using different odds providers and different approaches to the market.

blocks.text: Why multiple bookmakers give you more surebets

Many bookmakers use the same odds platform and therefore have near-identical prices. Surebets most often arise between bookmakers that set odds in their own different ways. If you only have accounts with bookmakers on the same platform, you'll see far fewer arbitrage betting opportunities.
What to look for

items: Licensed by the gambling regulator in your own country, so you're protected and can check the tax treatment of your winnings under your local rules.
Fast deposits and withdrawals, so you can move money where it's needed.
Wide range of sports and markets, especially tennis, football and basketball.
Competitive odds and low bookmaker margin on popular markets.
A welcome bonus with reasonable terms that you can clear using surebets.

blocks.text: How to build your bookmaker portfolio

Start with five to eight bookmakers that are licensed where you live, spread across different platforms. Well-known operators such as bet365, Pinnacle, Unibet, Betfair, William Hill, Betway and bwin are examples, but only use those that hold a licence in your country. This gives you a good range of opportunities without having to manage too many balances. Once you've got the routine down, you can expand with more.
In BetTrackerAI you can select exactly which bookmakers you have accounts with, so you only see surebets you can actually place.
Bookmakers with their own odds are worth their weight in gold

Bookmakers that set their own odds instead of buying them often react more slowly or differently to news. This is precisely where the price differences arise. On the flip side, they're also often the quickest to limit winning accounts through gubbing.

faq.q: How many bookmakers do I need for surebets?
faq.a: A good starting point is five to eight regulated bookmakers that are licensed where you live. The more different odds platforms you cover, the more surebets you'll have access to.

faq.q: Can I use unlicensed bookmakers for arbitrage betting?
faq.a: It's not recommended. Bookmakers without a licence in your jurisdiction may be blocked, and winnings from them may be subject to different tax treatment or lack regulatory protection. Always check the rules where you live, including local tax rules on betting winnings.

skat-paa-spillegevinster.title: Tax on gambling winnings – international betting guide
skat-paa-spillegevinster.metaTitle: Tax on Gambling Winnings – What You Need to Know
skat-paa-spillegevinster.description: Do you need to pay tax on betting winnings and surebets? Learn how tax rules work for licensed and offshore bookmakers, and what to document.
skat-paa-spillegevinster.intro: In some regulated markets, the answer is straightforward: winnings from licensed bookmakers are tax-free for the player, because the bookmaker pays duty to the state, not you. But tax on betting winnings differs from country to country, so the rules depend on where you live and where you bet. Always check your local rules.

blocks.text: Licensed bookmakers: check your local rules

When you bet with a provider licensed by the gambling regulator in your own country, the provider usually pays gambling duty on their revenue. In some countries this means your winnings are tax-free and don't need to be reported to your tax authority, but this is not the case everywhere. Only use bookmakers, such as bet365, Pinnacle, Unibet, Betfair, William Hill, Betway or bwin, where they are licensed in the country where you live, and always check the current tax rules there.
Offshore bookmakers without a local licence

If you bet with providers that do not hold a licence in your jurisdiction, the winnings may be taxable, and using them may not be legal at all. The rules depend on factors such as whether the provider holds a licence in another country and your own tax residence. This is one reason why it's often simpler to stick with bookmakers licensed where you live.
Does this apply to surebets too?

Yes. For tax purposes, a surebet is generally treated as two or three ordinary bets. Whether you're placing sure bets, value bets or standard bets, the same tax rules in your country normally apply. Check your local rules to see how winnings from licensed bookmakers are treated.
Keep a record of your bets. It makes it easy to document where the money comes from if your bank or tax authority asks.
Professional gambling

If betting is your main occupation on a substantial scale, different rules may apply in certain jurisdictions. If you're unsure about your own situation, contact your local tax authority or a qualified accountant.

faq.q: Do I need to pay tax on winnings from licensed bookmakers?
faq.a: It depends on your country. In some regulated markets, winnings from locally licensed providers are tax-free for the player, while in others they may be taxable. Check the current tax rules where you live.

faq.q: How can I see if a bookmaker is licensed in my country?
faq.a: The gambling regulator in your own country will have a list of approved providers on its website, and licensed bookmakers usually display the regulator's logo on their site.

bankroll-management.keyword: bankroll management guide for sports betting
bankroll-management.intro: Good bankroll management means deciding in advance how much money is dedicated to betting, how much you stake per bet and how the money is split across bookmakers. For value betting, stake 1–2% of your bankroll per bet. For surebets, the limit is liquidity: your money must sit at the right bookmakers when a surebet appears. Track everything to measure ROI.

blocks.text: Bankroll management: the basic rules

items: **Separate money:** your bankroll is money you can afford to lose and is kept apart from everyday finances.
**Fixed stake rules:** decide the stake size before you bet, not on gut feeling.
**No chasing losses:** raising stakes after a loss is the fastest way to empty a bankroll.
**Review monthly:** adjust stakes up or down based on your bankroll, not on one good week.

blocks.text: Stake sizing for value bets and surebets
Value bets can lose, so the stake must be small enough to survive losing streaks. Surebets do not lose when executed correctly, so the risk is execution: odds changes, voids and missing legs.

**Drawdown:** spot losing periods early and lower stakes in time.

faq.q: How big should my bankroll be for surebets?
faq.a: Many start with €1,000–€3,000 spread across 4–6 bookmakers. Less works, but the profit per surebet becomes very small.

faq.q: What percentage should I stake on value bets?
faq.a: 1–2% of your bankroll per bet is a common, conservative rule. Larger stakes increase the risk of ruin during losing streaks.

faq.q: How do I calculate ROI on my bets?
faq.a: Divide net profit by total stakes. €370 profit on €18,500 staked gives an ROI of 2.0%.

arbitrage-betting.title: How does arbitrage betting work? Lock in profit on every result
arbitrage-betting.metaTitle: How Does Arbitrage Betting Work? Guide 2026
arbitrage-betting.description: How arbitrage betting works: the formula, worked examples in €, and how to place your first surebet step by step for a locked-in profit.
arbitrage-betting.intro: Arbitrage betting works by backing every outcome of the same event at different bookmakers when the sum of the inverse odds is below 1. You split your stake so the payout is identical whatever happens. The gap between total stake and payout is your profit, usually 1–3% per surebet, secured by maths rather than luck.

blocks.text: Surebets explained: when two bookmakers disagree on price

Every bookmaker sets its own odds and builds in a margin of 4–7%. But they react at different speeds to injuries, line-ups and big bets. When one bookmaker is slow to cut a price while another has already raised the opposite outcome, the two prices together leave a surplus. That is a surebet. New to the concept? Start with [what surebets are](/en/guides/what-are-surebets).
The test is simple: calculate 1 ÷ odds for each outcome and add them up. If the total is below 1.00, you have an arbitrage. The lower the total, the bigger the profit.

blocks.title: Example: two-way tennis match, total stake €1,000
blocks.note: The total is below 1, so you make about €24.78 regardless of who wins the match.

blocks.text: Arbitrage betting guide: three outcomes in football

Football has home win, draw and away win. The principle is the same, you just need three prices and often three bookmakers. Because the margin is spread over three outcomes, 1X2 surebets are rarer and the profit tends to be a little lower than in tennis.

blocks.title: Example: Premier League match, total stake €2,000

blocks.text: How to place surebets: by hand or with a scanner

In theory you can compare odds across a dozen browser tabs, but surebets often last only a few minutes. By the time you have done the maths, the price has usually moved. That is why most bettors use an odds scanner that compares bookmakers continuously. Read more about how to [find surebets automatically](/en/guides/find-surebets-automatically).

items: **By hand:** free, but slow, and you rarely get there before the price changes.
**With a scanner:** surebets appear with the stake split already calculated, so you can act immediately.
**Calculator:** whichever method you use, check the stakes in the [surebet calculator](/en/calculator) before placing.

blocks.text: Risk-free bets in practice: five steps to your first surebet

items: **1. Open accounts** with at least two bookmakers licensed in the country where you live, ideally more, and deposit in advance.
**2. Find a surebet** where the sum of inverse odds is below 1.00.
**3. Calculate the stakes** so the payout is equal on every outcome.
**4. Place both bets quickly,** starting with the price most likely to move.
**5. Check your bet slips:** market, line and odds must match your calculation exactly.

blocks.text: The maths is risk-free; the execution is not always. **Odds moving** while you place the second bet, **voided bets** on obvious pricing errors and **limited accounts** are the real risks. Keep stakes moderate at first and read how to [avoid bookmaker limits](/en/guides/avoid-bookmaker-limits).
Want to see live surebets with the stakes already worked out? [BetTracker AI](/en) scans the bookmakers for you and shows surebets in real time.

faq.q: Is arbitrage betting legal?
faq.a: Yes, betting on every outcome of an event is not illegal in most countries. Bookmakers can still limit your account. Only use bookmakers licensed where you live, and check your local rules, including any tax on winnings. See [are surebets legal?](/en/guides/are-surebets-legal)

faq.q: How much can you make with surebets?
faq.a: A typical surebet returns 1–3% of the total stake. With €1,000 per surebet, 40 surebets a month and an average of 1.5%, that is roughly €600 a month.

faq.q: How many bookmakers do I need?
faq.a: At least two, but the more accounts you have, the more surebets you can take. Many arbers work with five to ten bookmakers.

faq.q: What if the odds change before my second bet?
faq.a: Recalculate the second bet at the new price. If the total is still below 1, you have a smaller surebet. If it is above, limit the loss by covering at the best price available.

hvad-er-surebets.title: What are surebets? How guaranteed odds work
hvad-er-surebets.metaTitle: What are surebets? Complete guide to arbitrage betting
hvad-er-surebets.description: Learn what surebets are, how they occur, and how you bet on all outcomes with different bookmakers to secure a guaranteed profit.
hvad-er-surebets.intro: A surebet – also called arbitrage betting or arbing – is a combination of odds across different bookmakers where you can bet on all possible outcomes of a match and still make a profit, regardless of how it ends. It sounds too good to be true, but it's pure mathematics.

blocks.text: Why do surebets exist?

Bookmakers set their odds independently of one another. They use different models, react differently to news and want to attract bets on particular outcomes. As a result, one bookmaker might offer high odds on the home team whilst another offers high odds on the away team. When the difference becomes large enough, a surebet occurs.

Surebets typically last only minutes. As soon as bookmakers adjust their odds, the opportunity disappears. That's why it requires either many hours of manual searching or a scanner that monitors the market continuously.
How to tell if it's a surebet
You calculate the inverse value of each odds (1 divided by the odds) and add them together. If the sum is below 1, you have a surebet. The lower the sum, the greater your profit.

blocks.title: Example: tennis with two outcomes
blocks.note: The sum is below 1, so this combination is a surebet.

blocks.text: How do you split your stake?

Your stake must be divided so that the payout is the same regardless of who wins. With a total stake of €1,000 in the example above, you place approximately €494 on player A and approximately €506 on player B. Both outcomes return approximately €1,037, meaning a profit of roughly €37.
You don't need to calculate this yourself. Our free sure bet calculator splits the stake automatically and shows your guaranteed profit.
What should you watch out for?

items: Odds can change whilst you're placing your bets. Place the bet with the most unstable odds first.
Check that the market is exactly the same at both bookmakers, such as whether extra time counts.
Keep funds at multiple bookmakers so you can act quickly.
Bookmakers may limit accounts that only bet on surebets. Read our guide on avoiding gubbing and account limits.

faq.q: Are surebets risk-free?
faq.a: Mathematically, the profit is guaranteed once both bets are placed at the correct odds. In practice, the risk lies in odds changing, cancelled bets or errors in the market.

faq.q: How much can you earn from surebets?
faq.a: Most surebets return between 1 and 5% of your stake. The profit comes from doing it many times, not from individual big wins.

faq.q: How do you find surebets?

dutching-betting.title: Dutching: how to split your stake across multiple outcomes
dutching-betting.metaTitle: Dutching betting – explanation, formula and example
dutching-betting.description: Dutching means splitting your stake across multiple outcomes so you get the same return regardless of which one wins. See the formula and an example.
dutching-betting.intro: Dutching is a betting method where you back multiple outcomes in the same event and distribute your stake so that you receive the same payout regardless of which of your selections wins. The method is particularly useful in tournaments and markets with many possible outcomes.

blocks.text: The difference between dutching and surebets

With a surebet you cover all outcomes and win regardless of the result. With dutching you only cover some of the outcomes. If one of them wins, you get the same return, but if none of them win, you lose your entire stake. Dutching is therefore not risk-free.
The formula
Calculate 1/odds for each outcome and add them together. Call the sum S. The stake on an outcome is the total stake times (1/odds) divided by S. The payout will be the total stake divided by S.

blocks.title: Example: three players in a tournament, total stake €1,000
rows: If one of the three wins
If none of the three win
blocks.note: The profit is only realised if one of your three players wins. You must judge for yourself how likely that is.

blocks.text: When does dutching make sense?

items: When you believe a few outcomes hold most of the probability, e.g. the three favourites in a tournament.
When you want to spread risk instead of backing a single outcome.
When you can get better odds at multiple bookmakers and want to distribute your stake between them.

blocks.text: Dutching is not a substitute for surebets. If you want guaranteed profit, you need to cover all outcomes at different bookmakers. The calculator shows the difference immediately.

faq.q: Is dutching the same as arbitrage betting?
faq.a: No. With arbitrage betting (surebets) you cover all outcomes and win regardless of the result. With dutching you only cover some of the outcomes and can lose your entire stake.

faq.q: Can you lose money on dutching?
faq.a: Yes. If none of the outcomes you've bet on win, you lose your entire total stake.

faq.q: How do you calculate dutching stakes?
faq.a: Add 1/odds together for your outcomes (S). The stake on each outcome is the total stake times 1/odds divided by S.

bookmakerens-margin.description: Bookmakers profit from a built-in margin in their odds. Learn to calculate it and find the bookmakers that give you the best odds.
bookmakerens-margin.intro: When you add up the implied probabilities from a market, the total comes to more than 100%. The excess is the bookmaker's margin, also called overround. It's the price you pay to bet.

blocks.text: How to calculate the margin
Calculate 1/odds for all outcomes in the market and add them together. Subtract 1 from the total and you have the margin.

blocks.title: Example: football match with odds 2.10, 3.40 and 3.60
blocks.note: Odds of 2.10 equate to 47.6%, but without the margin the true probability is approximately 45.4%.

blocks.text: Why does the margin matter?

The lower the margin, the better odds you get for the same probability. Over many bets, the difference between 3% and 7% makes a significant difference to your bankroll. So compare margins at the bookmakers you use on the markets you bet most. Margin and surebets

A surebet arises when the best odds from multiple bookmakers together give a total below 1. The bookmakers' margin is then more than offset by their disagreement on price. That's what a scanner looks for.
Use our calculator to enter odds and see the total straight away. If it's below 1, you have a surebet.

faq.q: What is a good bookmaker margin?
faq.a: The lower, the better. On popular football markets a margin of 3–6% is typical, and smaller leagues and specialist markets often have higher margins.

faq.q: What is overround?
faq.a: Overround is the English term for the bookmaker's margin, i.e. how much the implied probabilities add up to over 100%.

asiatisk-handicap.title: Asian Handicap Explained: Whole, Half and Quarter Lines
asiatisk-handicap.metaTitle: Asian Handicap Explained – Simple Guide with Examples
asiatisk-handicap.description: Understand Asian handicap: what -0.5, -1 and -0.25 mean, when you get your stake back, and why the line matters when placing surebets.
asiatisk-handicap.intro: Asian handicap is a football betting market where the draw is eliminated or split. This creates just two outcomes, which is why it's often used by those looking for surebets and arbitrage betting opportunities.

blocks.text: Whole lines: stake returned on draw

With a handicap of 0 or a whole number, your stake can be returned. Home team 0 means you get your money back if the match ends in a draw. Home team -1 means the team must win by at least two goals to return a profit. If they win by exactly one goal, you get your stake back.
Half lines: no stake returned
At -0.5, the team must win. A draw or loss results in a lost bet. At +0.5, you win if the team wins or draws. It's always either a win or a loss, and the stake is never returned.
Quarter lines: stake split in two
At -0.25, the stake is split in two: half on 0 and half on -0.5. At +0.25, it's half on 0 and half on +0.5. The result can therefore be a half win or a half loss.

blocks.title: Home team -0.25 with €100 stake
blocks.note: With +0.25 on the away team, it's reversed: a draw gives a win on one half and the stake back on the other.

blocks.text: Asian handicap and surebets

Because the market has two outcomes, you can combine home team -0.5 at one bookmaker with away team +0.5 at another and only need two bookmakers for a surebet. Make sure both sides have the corresponding line: -0.5 pairs with +0.5, and -0.25 pairs with +0.25.
Always check the line before placing a surebet. A difference of a quarter line can turn a guaranteed win into a risky bet.

faq.q: What does Asian handicap -0.5 mean?
faq.a: The team must win the match to return a profit. A draw or loss results in a lost bet.

faq.q: Do I get my stake back with Asian handicap?
faq.a: With whole lines, such as 0 or -1, you get your stake back if the match result exactly matches the handicap. With half lines this never happens, and with quarter lines you can get a half win or half loss.

roi-betting.title: ROI on betting: how to calculate your return
roi-betting.metaTitle: ROI Betting – How to Calculate Return on Your Bets
roi-betting.description: Learn to calculate ROI and yield on betting with examples. See what a good return is, and why ROI tells you more than your total profit.
roi-betting.intro: ROI stands for return on investment and shows how many per cent you earn relative to what you've staked. It's the figure that tells you whether your strategy works, regardless of how large your stakes are.

blocks.text: The formula
ROI = profit divided by total stake, multiplied by 100. Profit is what you've been paid out, minus what you've staked.

blocks.title: Example: a month of sure bets
blocks.note: You've earned 2.5 cents for every euro you've staked.

blocks.text: ROI and yield are the same thing

In betting, the terms ROI and yield are often used for the same figure: profit relative to total stake. Some instead calculate ROI relative to your bankroll. That gives a higher figure, because the same bankroll is used many times over. Always check which method a figure has been calculated with before comparing.
What is a good ROI?

items: Ordinary bets in the long term: most punters sit below 0%, because the bookmaker takes a margin.
Value betting: 2–5% over many bets is a good result.
Sure bets: typically 1–5% per sure bet, but almost without risk, because all outcomes are covered.

blocks.text: ROI is most meaningful over many bets. After 20 bets, the figure can swing a lot. After several hundred bets, it shows whether your strategy holds up.

faq.q: How do I calculate ROI on betting?
faq.a: Take your profit, divide by your total stake and multiply by 100. If you've staked €10,000 and earned €300, your ROI is 3%.

faq.q: What's the difference between ROI and profit?
faq.a: Profit is the amount you've earned. ROI is profit as a percentage of your stake. It makes it possible to compare results with different stakes.

blocks.text: Sports arbitrage: why the profit is guaranteed

A bookmaker makes money because its prices add up to more than 100% probability. When two bookmakers rate the same event differently, you take the best price on a different outcome at each one. live-arbitrage-betting-scanner.intro: A live arbitrage betting scanner compares in-play odds across bookmakers while matches are running and flags surebets the moment prices diverge. blocks.text: Live surebets: why in-play creates more opportunities

Before kick-off, prices move slowly. In play, every event shifts the probabilities instantly. A bookmaker that uses a slower data feed, or suspends markets for a few seconds longer, ends up with a price that no longer matches the rest of the market. That gap is a live surebet.

items: **Tennis:** a break of serve changes the odds dramatically, and bookmakers update at different speeds.
**Football:** goals, red cards and penalties create brief price gaps in 1X2 and over/under markets.

blocks.text: Bet delays and suspended markets: the live risks
Live betting adds risks that do not exist pre-match. Bookmakers use a bet delay of 3–10 seconds, during which the price can change or the bet can be rejected.

items: **Bet delay:** your bet is only accepted after a few seconds. If the price moves, it may be rejected.
**Suspended markets:** after a goal or a break, markets close briefly. Never place the first leg while the second market is suspended.
**Partial acceptance:** some bookmakers accept only part of your stake live. Check the confirmation before placing the second leg.
**Recalculate quickly:** if the second leg moves, recalculate in the [surebet calculator](/en/calculator) and cover at the best price available.

blocks.text: Place the leg at the bookmaker with the longest bet delay first. Once it is accepted, place the second leg at the faster bookmaker.

items: **Update every few seconds:** live prices older than 10 seconds are useless.
**Show the price age:** so you can see how fresh the surebet is.
**Filter live and pre-match separately:** live surebets need a different approach and lower stakes at first.
**Log every bet:** live results vary more, so a [bet tracker](/en/guides/bet-tracker) is essential to see if you are actually profitable.

faq.q: Are live surebets more profitable than pre-match?
faq.a: There are more of them, but margins are often smaller and the execution risk is higher. The net result depends on how fast and accurate you are.

faq.q: How fast do I need to be?
faq.a: Live surebets often last 10–60 seconds. You should be able to place both legs within that window, so have accounts funded and logged in beforehand.

faq.q: Do bookmakers limit live arbers faster?
faq.a: Often yes, because live arbing on slow prices is easy to spot. Mix in normal bets and read how to [avoid bookmaker limits](/en/guides/avoid-bookmaker-limits).

blocks.text: Value betting: what +EV actually means
A value bet is a bet where the odds are higher than the true probability justifies. You can lose any single value bet, but over hundreds of bets the positive expected value turns into profit.

blocks.title: Example: expected value on a single bet
blocks.note: Expected profit is an average. Actual results swing above and below it, especially over a small number of bets.

blocks.text: AI odds scanner: how fair odds are calculated

Sharp bookmakers have low margins and adjust quickly to professional money, so their prices are the best estimate of the true probability. The AI removes the margin from the sharp price and calculates fair odds.

blocks.title: Example: removing the margin from sharp odds

items: **Market matching:** AI recognises identical events and lines across bookmakers.
**Speed:** prices are recalculated every few seconds as markets move.
**Filtering:** the scanner ignores tiny edges and suspicious outliers that are likely to be voided.

blocks.text: AI sports betting: value bets vs surebets

items: **Surebets:** guaranteed profit on every result, but small margins and fast limits.
**Value bets:** single bets with higher expected profit, but with variance and losing streaks.
**Combine them:** many bettors use surebets for steady profit and value bets to increase ROI.

blocks.text: Read the full comparison of [value betting vs surebets](/en/guides/value-bets-vs-surebets).
AI betting in practice: rules that protect you

items: **Stake 1–2% of your bankroll** per value bet. See [bankroll management](/en/guides/bankroll-management).
**Minimum edge of 2–3%** to leave room for errors in the fair odds estimate.
**Track closing odds:** beating the closing line consistently is the best sign that your bets have value.
**Judge after hundreds of bets**, never after one week.

faq.q: Does AI guarantee profit on value bets?
faq.a: No. AI finds bets with positive expected value, but individual bets can lose. Profit comes over a large number of bets.

faq.q: How much can I make with value betting?
faq.a: A realistic long-term ROI is often 2–5% of turnover, depending on edge, bookmakers and how long your accounts stay open.

faq.q: Do bookmakers limit value bettors?
faq.a: Yes, soft bookmakers often limit customers who beat the closing line. Read how to [avoid bookmaker limits](/en/guides/avoid-bookmaker-limits).
